correctness.rationale: For the fixed x0>0 and k>1 in RESULT.md:15–25, the Euler update makes the signed error exactly the sum of the reciprocal defects h_j²x_j/(1+h_j x_j) minus 1/x_N. Before the cap, x_j^(-1/2) drops by ε/(2√(2k)) times 1+O(√ε) uniformly; the cap is crossed at x_j^(-1/2)=O(√ε). The leading number of uncapped steps is thus 2√(2k/x0)/ε with O(ε^(-1/2)) remainder. Each uncapped defect is ε²/(2k) times 1+O(√ε). After the cap, the reciprocal drops by at least ε^(3/2)/(2√2) per step over a distance at most kε, and the defects are bounded by ε²/2 each. The terminal reciprocal is ε+O(ε^(3/2)) because the relative overshoot is O(√ε). This gives both constants and the unique admissible cancellation at k=2/x0 for 0<x0<2; x0=2 would require the excluded k=1. At tuning only the stated upper bound on the remaining error is proved. Independent numerical recurrence checks corroborate both signed bias and work in four parameter regimes at three tolerances, not the asymptotic theorem. value.rationale: For the published quadratic benchmark, the signed defect separates accumulated slow Euler growth from the missing terminal tail and yields a practical parameter criterion for higher-order bias at unchanged inverse-tolerance work order. It also identifies when that improvement is inadmissible and quantifies the leading work constant, rather than claiming the same work prefactor for all k. The benefit is specific to this ODE and stopping rule.
